name: Daytona

modes.label: Sandbox, container class (default)
modes.note: Default Linux container class. Same published rates as the Linux VM class (vm-tier): billing docs list one reserved vCPU/RAM/disk meter for container, VM and GPU sandboxes; pricing page has no separate VM line. Container class: no pause, no fork, filesystem-only (cold) snapshots, no nested virtualization; auto-stops after 15 min idle and auto-archives after 7 days stopped (free). Billed on reserved vCPU/RAM per second incl. Creating/Starting/Stopping transitions. Idle tail: auto-stop default 15 min after last external activity (background processes don't count). Per-sandbox max 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 10 GiB disk by default org limit (raisable per region / Enterprise). Stopped = disk only; archived (auto after 7 d stopped) = free. Basis verified 2026-09-28: "Sandboxes are billed for the resources reserved: vCPU, RAM, and disk" (https://www.daytona.io/docs/en/billing/). Auto-stop default 15 min; "Merely having a script or background task running is not sufficient to keep the sandbox alive" (https://www.daytona.io/docs/en/sandboxes.md).
modes.perf_source: Container class only (split from the Linux VM class 2026-09-28). ComputeSDK (github.com/computesdk/benchmarks results/): cold_start 988.15 ms = sequential TTI 2026-08-07 on Daytona default sandbox (no snapshot; default container class); burst 341.39 ms = burst TTI 2026-09-25 and dax 69.2 s = DAX 2026-09-25, both on snapshot daytona-8cpu-16gb (since 2026-08-13), class inferred container (guest saw 64 host CPUs / 755 GiB). Burst swung 0-96 composite across Aug-Sep runs. The container class was never CPU-benchmarked by HPC (daytona-container pending).

modes.label: Linux VM sandbox (same rates; KVM / nested virt per-org feature)
modes.note: Linux VM sandbox class (snapshots daytona-vm-small/medium/large = 1/1/3, 2/4/8, 4/8/10 vCPU/GiB/GiB disk). Billed at the same reserved vCPU/RAM/disk meter as containers (https://www.daytona.io/docs/en/billing: one table for container, VM and GPU sandboxes; pricing page lists no separate Linux VM rate). VM-only: pause/resume, fork (filesystem + memory), hot snapshots, and nested virtualization: "Nested virtualization exposes KVM (/dev/kvm) inside the guest" via kvm=true at create, "linux-vm snapshots only. Requires the sandbox_kvm feature for the organization" (how an org gets it is undocumented; forking a KVM sandbox returns 403 if not enabled). Auto-pauses after 60 min idle by default and cannot be archived (paused disk billed; memory state not billed). No Dockerfile/declarative builds for VM snapshots (image reference only). Hypervisor not documented. Billed on reserved vCPU/RAM per second incl. Creating/Starting/Stopping/Pausing transitions.
modes.perf_source: Linux VM class only. cpu_runs_s 18.6: hpc-sandbox-benchmarks (branch provider/ascii-box, docs/results/2026-08-24-cpu), row from July CI run 30019301067 (2026-07-23), Daytona Linux VM class (snapshot baked SandboxClass.LINUX_VM), region us-west-2, 4 vCPU / 8 GiB. Same row as boat.dev/compare "Daytona 18.6". No TTI/DAX measured on the VM class.

modes.label: Windows VM sandbox (presets small/medium/large)
modes.note: Superseded by the separate daytona-windows card (Windows price read as additive: .0504 + .0858 = .1362/vCPU-h, per the pricing page listing OS Windows as its own line). Pricing page lists 'OS Windows $0.0858/vCPU/h'. Encoded as replacement reading: 0.0504 + 0.0354 surcharge = 0.0858/vCPU-h. If instead additive (0.0504 + 0.0858 = 0.1362), costs are higher — unverified. Presets fix RAM at 4 GiB/vCPU and disk at 30/50/50 GiB (windows-small 1/4/30, medium 2/8/50, large 4/16/50); disk above 5 GiB billed.

modes.label: GPU sandbox, on-demand
modes.note: Only for GPU workloads. GPU $ per GPU-hour; vCPU/RAM/disk metered on top at standard rates (per third-party gpuadvisor.com, not stated in official docs). Up to 8 GPUs; each GPU allows up to 16 vCPU / 192 GB RAM / 512 GB disk (max_vcpu/ram above = 8 GPUs). Ephemeral: deleted on stop (no pause/persistence). Runs in virtual 'earth' region (region ignored). Free credits NOT usable. B200 is on pricing page but not in docs GPU type list. GPU sandboxes have their own per-GPU limits (16 vCPU / 192 GB RAM / 512 GB disk per GPU), so the CPU tiers’ 4 vCPU / 8 GiB org limits do not apply. B300 on-demand corrected 6.25 -> 7.10 (2026-09-28, rendered on-demand tab of https://www.daytona.io/pricing; 6.25 was the B200 figure; spot/on-demand ratio 0.575 matches the other SKUs).

modes.label: GPU sandbox, spot / preemptible
modes.commit_note: Preemptible: can be terminated at any time without notice when on-demand needs capacity; not counted against GPU quota.
modes.note: Only for GPU workloads tolerant of eviction (spotEvictedAt recorded, sandbox retrievable 24 h after eviction). Launched v0.205.0 (2026-08-18). ~35-43% below on-demand GPU rates; CPU/RAM assumed same as on-demand. Free credits NOT usable. GPU sandboxes have their own per-GPU limits (16 vCPU / 192 GB RAM / 512 GB disk per GPU), so the CPU tiers’ 4 vCPU / 8 GiB org limits do not apply.

plans.name: Tier 1 (email verified)
plans.note: Concurrency is an org-wide pool (10 vCPU / 20 GiB / 30 GiB disk per https://www.daytona.io/docs/en/limits, re-checked 2026-09-28), not a sandbox count. 300 creates/min. Restricted egress (allowlisted essential services only).

plans.name: Tier 2 (card + $25 top-up)
plans.note: One-time $25 prepaid top-up (spent as credit). 400 creates/min. Egress still restricted.

plans.name: Tier 3 ($500 top-up)
plans.note: One-time $500 prepaid top-up (spent as credit). 500 creates/min. Full internet access; VPN integrations.

plans.name: Tier 4 ($2,000 top-up every 30 days)
plans.note: Recurring $2,000 prepaid top-up every 30 days = de facto $2k/month minimum spend consumed as usage credit. 600 creates/min.

plans.name: Enterprise / dedicated or custom (BYOC) region
plans.note: Contact sales: custom limits, SSO/SCIM, audit logs, dedicated single-tenant regions, BYOC runners (unbounded by quota). Volume discounts unpublished.

features.ip_note: Egress IP type not documented; outbound traffic can be routed via a customer HTTP(S) proxy (outboundProxyUrl) or VPN (Tailscale/OpenVPN/Netbird).

perf_source: Two measured runtimes (container default, Linux VM class): perf is per mode.

knobs.label: Auto-stop idle tail, containers (x session hours)
knobs.why: Container sandboxes bill reserved vCPU/RAM until auto-stop fires, default 15 min after the last external activity (background processes don't count). Factor = (session + tail) / session: default 15 min on 30-min sessions = 1.5x; 1 if you stop sandboxes explicitly.

knobs.label: Auto-pause idle tail, Linux VMs (x session hours)
knobs.why: Linux VM sandboxes auto-pause after 60 min idle by default (4x the container tail) and bill full vCPU/RAM until then. Factor = (session + tail) / session: 60 min on 30-min sessions = 3x.

caveats: Plans carry extra non-spec keys pool_vcpu/pool_ram_gib/pool_disk_gib: Daytona concurrency is an org-wide resource pool per region, not a sandbox count (concurrency left null).

Linux VM class is billed at the same meter as containers (billing docs; no separate VM line on the pricing page). 2026-09-28: re-split into two modes with identical rates because features differ: on-demand = container (no pause/fork, fs-only snapshots, no nested virt), vm-tier = Linux VM (pause, fork, memory snapshots, /dev/kvm). Card-level features describe the best available class; mode.features carry the per-class truth.
Windows $0.0858/vCPU-h encoded as replacing the Linux vCPU rate; if additive, Windows vCPU would cost $0.1362/h.
GPU: vCPU/RAM/disk billed on top of GPU rate per third-party tracker, not stated in official docs. Free credits not usable on GPU.
Snapshot storage 'remains billed' but rate unpublished (null). Warm-pool idle billing undocumented.
Egress/ingress pricing not published; treated as unknown (null). No public IPv4 offered.
Billed transitions (Creating/Starting/Stopping/Pausing) have unknown duration (boot_overhead_s null).
Idle tail billed: containers keep billing until 15-min idle auto-stop, VMs until 60-min auto-pause; background processes do not count as activity.
Stopped/paused disk billed indefinitely except archived containers (auto-archive after 7 d stopped by default). 5 free GiB assumed per sandbox (unverified).
Tier 1-2 have restricted outbound internet; full internet requires Tier 3 ($500 prepaid top-up).
Per-sandbox default max 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 10 GiB disk (raisable per region); disk can never shrink.
$200 free credit is one-time; expiry term exists but unpublished. Startup credits: pricing page says up to $50k, startups page up to $100k.
Volume discounts and Enterprise/dedicated/BYOC pricing unpublished.

Verifier 2026-09-28: the engine ignores pool_vcpu/pool_ram_gib/pool_disk_gib and all tiers have concurrency null, so it always picks a $0 tier. A fleet needing >250 vCPU / >500 GiB concurrently really requires Tier 4 ($2,000 top-up every 30 days, a de facto usage floor), and Tier 1-2 cannot reach the open internet; neither is enforced by the estimate.
Creation rate limits per tier (300/400/500/600 per min, https://www.daytona.io/docs/en/limits) are not modelled.

Verifier 2026-09-28: https://www.daytona.io/pricing (static render) shows only the preemptible GPU column (matching the spot mode); on-demand GPU prices are primary-sourced from a Chrome render of the pricing page's On-demand tab (2026-09-28, research/raw/daytona-On-demand.txt: B300 $7.10, B200 $6.25, MI355X $5.99, H200 $4.54, H100 $3.95); the static fetch shows only the preemptible column. The pricing page lists Windows as a separate 'OS, Windows $0.0858/vCPU/h' line, which reads like an additive surcharge (reading B); the card keeps reading A (replacement) - unresolved.
perf is mode-level (card-level nulled): on-demand (container) carries ComputeSDK TTI/DAX; vm-tier (Linux VM) carries the HPC CPU result (18.6 runs/s). See research/perf-map.json.

Open source: the public daytonaio/daytona repository states that as of June 2026 core development moved to a private codebase and the repo receives no further updates, fixes or releases. Historical v0.190.0 code remains AGPLv3; it is not the current managed service. Sources: https://github.com/daytonaio/daytona/blob/ec4c21b2d597091ac09ecc278f3bcc172575a987/README.md , https://github.com/daytonaio/daytona/blob/v0.190.0/LICENSE

2026-09-28 (docs/limits): org-wide pools Tier 1 10 vCPU / 20 GiB / 30 GiB (was recorded as 10 GiB RAM), Tier 2 100/200/300, Tier 3 250/500/2,000, Tier 4 500/1,000/5,000; creates/min 300/400/500/600. Encoded as plan max_total_vcpu / max_total_ram_gib (not yet enforced by the engine) and max_starts_per_min (enforced). Snapshot storage rate still unpublished (null).

2026-09-28 features: nested virtualization (/dev/kvm) only on Linux VM sandboxes created with kvm=true, and only if the org has the sandbox_kvm feature (enablement path undocumented). Container, GPU and Windows classes: no nested virt. Desktop: VNC/xfce4 desktop is in the default container image and Linux VM/Windows run at a fixed VNC resolution; custom images need the packages installed; GPU class desktop unknown (null). Docker-in-Docker documented for sandboxes (docker:dind snapshots, Docker Compose).

Wall-clock TTL (v0.199.0, 2026-07-17): optional per-sandbox ttl_minutes destroys the sandbox in any state after a fixed deadline. It is disabled by default, so max_session_h stays null. It serves as a per-sandbox runaway-cost guard, not an org-level cap.

Top-ups are prepaid wallet credit and non-refundable. The Tier 2/3/4 thresholds ($25, $500, $2,000 every 30 days) are therefore sunk cash if the usage is not consumed, and a negative balance can suspend the org. Expiry and rollover of paid credit are not published. SLA service credits apply only to Tier 4 and above.

Rate limits per tier (docs/limits): general API 10k/20k/40k/50k per min; sandbox creation 300/400/500/600 per min; lifecycle ops (start/stop/etc.) 10k/20k/40k/50k per min. max_starts_per_min holds the creation limit, so restarting existing sandboxes is far less constrained.

fleet.verification: Tier 1 email verification; Tier 2 linked credit card plus $25 top-up; Tier 3 $500 top-up; Tier 4 $2,000 top-up every 30 days. No universal ID/business-doc requirement stated.
fleet.tiers: Default-region aggregate pools: T1 10 vCPU/10 GiB/30 GiB disk; T2 100/200/300; T3 250/500/2,000; T4 500/1,000/5,000. Custom via support@daytona.io.
fleet.notes: No fixed sandbox count: fleet depends on all three resource pools, retained container disk and warm pools. At 4 vCPU/8 GiB CPU/RAM alone supports at most 1/25/62/125 per tier, with disk potentially tighter. Thus 300/1,000 of that size need custom quota. T1/T2 restrict egress. GPU quotas are class/Earth-region-specific and not numerically published; spot GPUs bypass quota but still require capacity. No approval SLA.
